aerial._doc: USDA NAIP 2022-04-25 (public domain), the whole-box z18 mosaic (source/naip_2022_lm_full_z18.md; Git LFS, sha256 1764a80b...). bbox = its 62 x 41 tiles from x 45801, y 105749 (its georef). The mosaic is Web Mercator and the bake reads an image as linear in latitude: over its 5,260 m north to south that is off by at most 0.35 m, at mid-height [measured on the georef], under one photo pixel and under the texel; the bake's own registration shift takes up what is common.

exclude.why: the Speedway lap's line along College's NORTHBOUND road (ledger 0055 round 2; race.laps.college), a plain connector record, so the paint rule read it as a two-way road with a centre yellow: 8 lanes (12 lane records, 2.7 km of lane line) laid over the split zone's own lanes for that 1.0 km of road, so its wheel paths were drawn twice and half of them against the traffic (the first trial bake's deepest rubber, 39.4 %, was two lanes' stripes multiplied). The split zone's reader supplies that road's lanes

lanes._dash_gap_doc: tools/road_lanes.py DASH GAPS (opt-in). Princess View's half carriageway is about 5.8-5.9 m between the yellow and the edge line, at the limit for two authored lanes, so its dashed divider flickers off for a row or a few; read as painted, lane 1 jogged 1.8 m outward there and, where lane 2 was welded across the gap, both lanes' wheel paths lay over the same space (the deepest rubber of the bake, 38.8 %, at Princess View row 207 and Jackson north row 617). A dashed divider's gap of at most 8 rows (24 m) between two painted rows is read as painted. 8 [invented]: the measured break (11 gaps of 1-8 rows, the rest 13 rows and longer, none at a side street) and two cycles of a 3 m dash and 9 m gap
lanes._ends_doc: tools/road_lanes.py LANE ENDS (opt-in). A lane that goes on in another record is welded to it (College's 12 joints at rows 1129 / 1130 and 1476 / 1477, 3 m apart; two authored lanes that drop out for two stations); every other open end fades over fade_m and is cut square, so no wheel path is drawn round a lane's end. fade_m 8.0 [invented]: two car lengths, where a driver leaves the lane's wheel paths for the turn, and over twice the wear band's 3.0 m reach, so the end reads as a fade. At a junction (the Mac 2026-11-23, ledger 0084 'Junction boxes and pads get the tone only'): no lane enters a pad and a side road's lanes stop at the through road's edge [measured], so pads and mouths carry the tone only, reached over the fade; a through road's own lanes run on through the box. Kevin's drive judges the length
lanes._doc: tools/road_lanes.py (ledger 0084's 'lanes' source): one line per lane, both directions, from the paint's own rule; the bake runs it and writes data/road_wear.lanes.json. College Ave's two one-way roads and their forks (rows 1130-1476) are read by read_college_split off the data the scene's rows were built to. Defaults: every connector, min_edge_lane_m 2.9 [invented], rubber 1.0 [invented]. 221 lane lines, 47.4 km forward and 49.4 km reverse once college_nb is left out (2026-11-23; the first trial bake had 233 with it).
